title: Break the Fake Movement to host the AI Literacy Summit 2026
summary: The future of AI literacy in the Philippines is about to take another step forward at the AI Literacy Summit
byline: Francis Christian Lubag, Paolo Miguel Ordonio

blocks.text: The future of AI literacy in the Philippines is about to take another step forward at the AI Literacy Summit 2026, on November 28, 2026, at the University of Santo Tomas in Manila, Philippines.

Following the successful program implementation and to celebrate our milestone along with the 2026 Global Media and Information Literacy Week, the Break the Fake Movement, in partnership with the University of Santo Tomas, organized the Summit to bring together youth, the academe, media, civil society organizations, and government institutions to dialogue about the future of AI literacy in the country.

The gathering comes on the heels of the AI Ready ASEAN Programme completion, which saw Break the Fake Movement successfully train more than 350,000 Filipinos on effective AI use and literacy. Across Southeast Asia, the program led to 9 million trained individuals.

With the theme “Continuing the Conversation on Shaping an Inclusive and Ethical AI Literacy for the Philippines,” the Summit will serve as an avenue to map AI literacy in the Philippines in light of public and private interventions over the years. Moreover, the event aims to chart a path forward for identifying core AI competencies, developing actionable strategies to integrate AI into learning and everyday practices, promoting ethical AI use, and strengthening digital resilience. Building on the outcomes and learnings from the AI Ready ASEAN Programme, the Summit aims to catalyze a multi-sectoral National AI Literacy Action Plan, directly reinforcing the country’s role as a regional leader in driving inclusive and human-centered digital innovation.

Driving the conversations are speakers and panelists from the ASEAN Foundation, the University of Santo Tomas, the AI Ready ASEAN Programme Local Implementing Partners and selected Master Trainers, the Department of Education, the Department of Information and Communications Technology, Safe AI Philippines, and MediaSmarts Canada.

Due to the limited onsite capacity, registration for in-person participation is now closed. You can still join the Summit virtually through a livestream. Follow Break the Fake Movement’s official social media page to catch the livestream of the event.
For more details about the Summit, you may contact btfm_programs@breakthefakemovement.com.
